items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I made the Clambake Seven songs with Yank Lawson... That was the begining of a beautiful thing --' recording wise and friendship wise, and a series of albums, running between 20 and 30.

ctx.x: I made the Clambake Seven songs with Yank Lawson, and I can't name you any specific numbers.

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I had talked into this machine... about the Lawson-Haggard band... we augmented the band... So I hope this might be inserted -- it was deleted. However, Bob Haggard and Lawson in doing the arrangements... we had the original which I mentioned

ctx.x: When the wonderful, great piano player, Ralph Sutton, visited my house, he looked at the picture and commented, "Where were your sixguns, Cliff?" and I said "Security wouldn't allow me".

And I need an insertion here. That was the Bicentennial that we were playing -- I left out the word 'bi', which was of course, nationwide -- rather, our nation's great celebration. I noticed that in playing this back, that I had talked into this machine, this fool machine here for 10 or 15 minutes about the Lawson-Haggard band, and upon our recording with a larger group, and I forgot to push all the proper buttons. So it was deleted. However, Bob Haggard and Lawson in doing the arrangements, wanted to enlarge…
And of course we added George Burns, who was working at that time on the Hit Parade. So I hope this might be inserted -- it's of importance to me.

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: the nucleus was that ank Lawson and Bob Haggart, naturally, and they were at a loss for a piano player... we went over to Lou Stein's house

ctx.x: Bob Haggart and I had done so many things that Bob Crosby got credit for, that we want to get together and organize a group. And was I interested.

And I naturally said yes, but I took it with a grain of salt because somebody's always saying, "Well, we're gonna do this and we're gonna do that". However, we were rehearsing at Lou St. 's house, and the nucleus was that ank Lawson and Bob Haggart, naturally, and they were at a loss for a piano player, and we went over to Lou Stein's house -- somebody suggested Lou, I did for one. He was a great player; I had been recording with Lou, and they didn't know if his style would fit in the group of what they had in…
Well, it did. And if you're acquainted with any of the great albums Lou made, God only knows I don't know who would have covered the situation any better.
